title: Canonical regularization of the stationary Coulomb problem and an Aufbau-like spectral ordering
abstract: The stationary hydrogen atom has Coulomb degeneracy across orbital levels, whereas the Aufbau/Madelung ordering is an empirical, many-electron rule established in atomic physics. We examine the hydrogen atom through a regularized de Broglie--Bohm representation, in which stationary amplitude current constraints generate separable Sturm--Liouville branches. In this formulation, the radial, orbital, and magnetic sectors acquire canonical Langer-like inverse square corrections. The modified boundary value problems allow analytical solutions and produce a hydrogen-like spectrum with regularized radial and angular indices. Consequently, radial Coulomb quantization acquires an orbital dependent shift, lifting the Coulomb degeneracy and producing a spectral ordering that follows the Aufbau/Madelung sequence.   On this basis, we construct the ordering of the regularized de Broglie--Bohm states and show that the spectral structure retains the standard degenerate Rydberg sequence in the l=0 sector. The separated amplitudes are represented by generalized special function branches, including the associated Laguerre, Legendre, and Bessel functions with non-integral parameters arising from regularized separation. Therefore, the treatment is intended as an analytical examination of spectral ordering in a regularized one center Coulomb problem rather than as a replacement for the many electron atomic structure theory.   Keywords: de Broglie--Bohm representation; Coulomb spectrum; canonical regularization; Langer correction; Sturm--Liouville equations; Aufbau principle; Madelung ordering; associated Legendre functions; associated Laguerre functions; Bessel functions.
summary: The paper analyzes the hydrogen atom using a regularized de Broglie-Bohm quantum mechanical framework. By imposing canonical constraints, the authors modify the standard radial and angular equations, leading to solutions involving generalized special functions with non-integral parameters. This regularization mathematically forces the energy spectrum to exhibit an Aufbau-like ordering for higher angular momentum states, lifting the inherent Coulomb degeneracy.
main_problem: To investigate whether canonical regularization of the stationary Coulomb problem can intrinsically generate an Aufbau/Madelung spectral ordering, thereby lifting the inherent degeneracy found in the standard hydrogen atom model.
main_result: The regularized spectrum yields a sequence that follows the Aufbau/Madelung order for higher angular momentum states, while the $l=0$ sector retains the standard degenerate Rydberg sequence.
method: The authors apply canonical regularization constraints to the de Broglie-Bohm representation of the Coulomb problem, leading to modified Sturm-Liouville equations solved using generalized special functions.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the one-center stationary Coulomb potential (hydrogen atom). The mathematical framework involves decomposing the wavefunction into amplitude and phase components within a regularized de Broglie-Bohm representation.
key_observables: The energy eigenvalues $E_{n,r,\lambda}$ are key observables; the spectral ordering itself is the primary result.
important_parameters: The regularization introduces non-integral parameters into the associated Laguerre, Legendre, and Bessel functions. The minimum labeling scheme $\lambda = l - 1/2$ is crucial for comparison.
main_assumptions: The treatment is explicitly limited to an analytical examination of spectral ordering in a regularized one-center problem, not a replacement for full many-electron atomic structure theory (which requires considering screening and correlation).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the energy $E_{n_r,\lambda}$ vs $\lambda$, showing symmetry around $\lambda = -1/2$ and mapping this minimum branch to the s-sector. Figure 2 compares the degenerate Rydberg energies with the shifted regularized spectrum, demonstrating the Aufbau order.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the mathematical framework by applying canonical regularization to the de Broglie-Bohm equations for the Coulomb problem. It then solves the resulting separated radial, orbital, and axial differential equations using generalized special functions. Finally, it analyzes the energy quantization condition derived from these solutions to map out the spectral ordering.
why_interesting: This work is theoretically interesting because it uses advanced mathematical techniques (de Broglie-Bohm formalism, canonical regularization) applied to a fundamental physical problem (Coulomb potential) to derive an emergent structure (Aufbau principle), providing a purely mathematical mechanism for spectral splitting.
